summary:
Seoul stands under the national framework of South Korea. The national provisions on criminal law, documents, military service and legal gender recognition are carried in that country record; what follows is specific to the Seoul jurisdiction.

On 2 July 2024 the Seoul Central District Court, presiding judge Chung In-jae, dismissed the state's appeal and made final a damages ruling in favour of plaintiff A against the state. The plaintiff was awarded 300,000 won of the 3 million won claimed. Neither party appealed, so the judgment stands without further review.

The court held that a police officer's advice to an LGBT person in the middle of a legal gender transition, telling them to avoid public restrooms for a period, infringed personal rights. It stated that the right to use restrooms comfortably is a fundamental and universal human right.

The finding is documented judicial protection against official interference with restroom access in Seoul, including advice issued by police to a person whose transition is visible to the authorities.
tangentialFactors:
Restroom access litigation has produced damages awards elsewhere in South Korea. In 2021 the Pohang branch of the Daegu District Court awarded 7 million won against an academy that had barred a trans student's restroom use, a separate jurisdiction whose practice is recorded here only for comparison.

The Seoul judgment is a claim against the state rather than against the individual officer who gave the advice, and the award was set well below the amount the plaintiff sought, at 300,000 won of 3 million won claimed.
localsOnly:
A Seoul resident who is advised by police to restrict their restroom use during a legal gender transition has a final judgment on record establishing that such advice infringes personal rights and is actionable for damages against the state.

The 300,000 won awarded on 2 July 2024 indicates the level of compensation a Seoul court assessed in a case where the claimant sought 3 million won, giving a concrete reference point for the value such a claim has been given.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Seoul courts apply the outdated national judicial guidelines that some courts still use to condition gender-marker change on sex reassignment surgery is not sourced here; the Seoul-specific inventory documents only the restroom ruling.

No Seoul-specific source in this inventory addresses municipal facility policy, transit facilities, or hospital admission practice for trans people in the city; those questions are unresolved for this jurisdiction.

National survey data on trans people's restroom avoidance, including the 2021 National Human Rights Commission of Korea findings, sits with the national record rather than this regional one and is not restated here.
